findings.title: Credential-shaped structured quality output crossed the durable evidence boundary
findings.originalExpected: Scan the fully serialized evidence object before durable commit, quarantine or fail closed on detection, prove that the object cannot be resolved, and add a regression test for credential material under an unremarkable structured key.
findings.originalObserved: Independent attack G4-X7 assembled a synthetic canonical scanner marker in memory, passed it through record_execution under an ordinary output key, and observed that the existing redaction missed it while the evidence store persisted and resolved it unchanged.
findings.rootCause: Runtime mapping redaction and the repository secret scanner owned different detection taxonomies, while QualityEvidenceStore trusted redacted input and began content-addressed lookup and persistence without scanning the exact serialized bytes.
implementation: packages/common now owns the canonical credential-shape taxonomy consumed by both ledger controls and the evaluator image.

QualityEvidenceStore scans exact serialized bytes before digest calculation, repository lookup, object stat, upload, or metadata commit; detection and scanner failure use stable fail-closed error codes.
Evidence resolution rescans downloaded bytes before accepting size and digest, so legacy or injected prohibited content cannot support a verdict.
record_execution catches only containment error codes and persists a sanitized ERROR result with no evidence or finding payload; pure verdict derivation returns FAIL.
ADR-0032, LSN-0091, and GRD-0092 make the boundary and its regression controls permanent.
negativeTest: G4-X7 sends a canonical scanner-detected marker under stdout, then requires ERROR, FAIL, zero object writes, zero metadata records, and absence from serialized result and verdict.
The scanner-failure mutation raises before any durable operation instead of treating an unavailable scanner as a clean scan.
